answer.rationale: With 18% spend reduction mandated and 14 days to contract renewal, switching vendors (memory_c2 shows prior success) was the first instinct. However, the assembly line runs at 94% capacity with zero buffer—switching introduces migration risk and integration uncertainty we cannot absorb. Renewing alone forfeits the cost target. Instead, negotiation offers a path: memory_c4 demonstrates the incumbent responds to benchmarking pressure; memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. Verification of these two will confirm whether renegotiation can bridge the 18% gap without switching. If the incumbent moves materially on price and terms, we renew and hit the mandate. If they do not, we have 14 days remaining to escalate to a vendor switch with full knowledge of what failed. This preserves optionality, respects the delivery risk constraint, and avoids binary commitment when cash pressure and capacity stress are both high. The second-source option (memory_c3) is valuable but absorbs time and capex we do not have this cycle.
